Additionally, the Nhan Noi Temple at number 84A Hang Bo Street also pays homage to Princess Lan Ngoc, and the Nhan Noi Communal House at number 33 Bat Dan Street is dedicated to the White Horse deity.

The village of Nhan Noi was formerly known as Hang Nui, suggesting that the area once had a thriving pottery industry, producing clay pots and utensils. The name "Hang Bo" itself is derived from the middle section of the street, where until the early French colonial era, shops selling various bamboo baskets and other woven goods were concentrated.

Around the turn of the 20th century, Hang Bo Street became home to many Chinese immigrants from Chaozhou, who engaged in rice and fruit trading, as well as operating photography studios. The street's rich history and cultural significance continue to attract visitors interested in exploring its traditional crafts, architecture, and the vibrant local life that thrives there.
